1kage3w:400: The NVIDIA driver supports serializing CUDA context state from GPU device memory to host memory, which is then transferred via the host-side checkpoint filesystem (ImageFS) and written back to GPU device state by the driver on the target machine upon restore. Key prerequisites: the best practice for vLLM/SGLang GPU snapshotting is to offload weights to the host before checkpointing, and to recreate the KV cache rather than restore it (rebuild is faster than restore); multi-GPU programs make snapshotting complex because of NCCL's collective communication design (a single silent GPU can deadlock the entire group). With these prerequisites met, vLLM's average cold start drops from 95,679ms to 13,797ms (7×), and SGLang's from 83,713ms to 17,486ms (4.8×).
1otckal:416: Traditional Docker image loading requires applying each layer sequentially and transferring the entire root filesystem (potentially several GB), even though most files are never read by the application. Modal's ImageFS does two things: first, the metadata (index files) is only a few MB, can be loaded ahead of the content, and completes within 100ms, allowing containers to begin execution before content is fully loaded; second, content-addressed caching (rather than Docker's path-based or layer-based caching) enables deduplication across containers—common dependencies like Python, PyTorch, and the CUDA stack can share the same physical data across different containers. The tiered cache (page cache → local SSD → AZ cache server → regional CDN → blob storage) ensures hot data is read from the fastest tier, with cold data percolating down from upper tiers on demand.

This means gVisor containers can naturally serialize their execution state into checkpoints without depending on kernel-level criu functionality. At the same time, gVisor's reduced attack surface (emulated kernel rather than real kernel) provides additional security isolation—Modal explicitly notes this makes their system naturally immune to certain kernel vulnerabilities (such as CVE-2026-31431 "CopyFail").
